title: 1Password will fill a login without showing the password to the agent
friendlyTitle: 1Password can sign an agent in without showing it the password
summary: 1Password has announced 1Password for Agents, a way for a personal agent to sign in without receiving or storing the password. When an agent reaches a sign-in form, it proves its identity to 1Password with a unique digital key. The person sees which credential is needed and why, then approves the request on their own device. 1Password fills the form itself. The company says it is building this with Muse, Claude, OpenAI, Grok Bot, and Town, and is also working with Browserbase, Perplexity, Ramp, and others. It points readers to its site for which integrations are actually available.

You approve that request on your own device. 1Password then fills the form itself. The company says it is building this with Muse, Claude, OpenAI, Grok Bot, and Town. whyItMatters: Pasting a password into a chat is how a copy ends up in a transcript, a memory, or a log you no longer control. An approval on your own device is a better default, if the integration for your agent is live. It is not a reason to let an agent move money. A bank can still treat the login as yours.
